image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on calm, dark water. The duck features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a greyish-brown body, and a bright yellow bill. One orange webbed foot is visible paddling beneath the water surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and bright yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible against the dark green head plumage and appears black/dark brown.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a swimming duck, appearing buoyant and streamlined. Plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the mallard pattern: iridescent green head, clear white neck ring, and grey/brown body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is visible underwater. It shows the correct anatomical position (set back) and the visible toes appear connected by webbing, consistent with a duck foot.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing typical feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, short and featuring the characteristic upward curl of the central feathers typical of male mallards.

To check for edge bleeding or melting between the duck's body and the water, a common AI artifact in floating subjects.
To analyze the fine details of the feathers for any smearing, repetition, or unnatural smoothness indicative of generative artifacts.

Anatomical correctness of the submerged webbed foot

Feather texture detail on the green head
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the submerged foot. AI often struggles with rendering webbed feet correctly, especially when partially obscured by water. Verify if the 'webbing' looks like a solid membrane or just fused toes. Also, check the transition between the green head and the white neck ring for any color bleeding.
